comment: Bug localisation on **Long Code Arena** (Bogomolov et al., arXiv 2406.11612), the authors' own test split.
**What the task is.** Given an issue and the repository at the commit where it reproduces, name the files that
must change. **The ground truth is the fixing commit**, so nobody wrote it by hand.
**The metric is the authors' own**, transcribed unchanged from
`lca-baselines/bug_localization/src/baselines/metrics/quality_metrics.py`: set-based precision, recall, F1, FPR,
all-correct, at-least-one-correct, all-incorrect, averaged over the instances that were measured.
**Two arms.** `retrieval` is the fused list cut at k with **no model involved** - free, deterministic, and a
change in it is a change in the retriever. `answer` is the file set the model *cited*, which is only produced
when a provider is present; it is the same ruler applied to a different thing.
**This is not the `filepath_imports` baseline reproduced.** That configuration shows the model every file path
and the import graph; this product shows it the blocks a hybrid retriever selected. The published baselines and
this figure answer the same question with different amounts of context, and the artifact reports the
configuration rather than implying equivalence.
**Why the retrieval arm leads with k and not with a chosen set size.** A set size picked after seeing the
ground truth is a fit. The cuts are fixed in advance and all of them are published.
**Why there are two controls.** The reading the product ships - a file is placed by its best two declarations
rather than by its best one - was chosen because its paired interval against BM25 excluded zero, and a choice
made against one comparator can be a fit to it. `crossCheck` ranks the identical index with TF-IDF, so the two
controls differ in the weighting formula and nothing else; `controlSummary` prints them one line each and the
gate refuses an artifact where they were not measured on the same instances.
**Why the figure is combined from parts.** One job measures one language split, because an analysis of a real
checkout costs megabytes of resident memory per file and V8 does not return reclaimed pages to the operating
system - three splits in one process was three times the accumulation, and that job never finished. **The
combination is a mean over the pooled rows**, so it equals what a single run would have produced, and
`byLanguage` shows which language moved.
**The published baselines are a MAP table, so a MAP column is published beside the cuts.** The paper reports
`GTE` 0.33, `Mistral` 0.30, `TF-IDF` 0.27, `BM25` under 0.25 and `GPT-4` 0.39, averaged over the same
three splits - so `overall.map` is the only column here that can be placed beside them without a conversion
somebody invented. **Two differences are stated rather than smoothed**: their figures are over all fifty
instances per split and this one is over the rows a runner reached, and average precision here reads the
retriever's own pool of two hundred candidates, which can only lose credit.

conditions.note: Retrieval baselines rank every file in the repository by cosine distance; the chat baselines name 1-5 files from the issue and the whole path list, chunked when it does not fit the context.

fileCap.reason: the cap admits 4000 files where the charge affords 1981 at 120 declarations per file, so a checkout between the two was measured under a bound that cannot pay for it - the wider cap is published rather than narrowed here, because narrowing it now would be editing the run instead of reporting it
fileCap.appliedTo: every file in the checkout except .git

memory.note: An instance is skipped when its checkout is above the stated cap or would end past the job’s time budget, and an instance whose analysis crosses the declaration guard is refused **inside the child process**, at the declaration where the graph would have grown past what the runner can pay for. **A measured instance ran in its own process**, which is killed at `instanceRssCapMb` and `instanceTimeoutMs`, so a refusal names the ceiling that fired rather than the runner disappearing.

density.note: Declarations per file, measured on this run’s own measured rows: `median` and the quantiles are over `rows`, which is why the denominator is published beside them. **The numerator is the whole checkout and the denominator is one extension**, so the ladder's rungs price a conversion between two populations rather than between two estimates of one. `chargedAtCovered` counts the rows whose declarations the shipped charge covers: the rest are charged less than they cost, and the process ceiling - not the rule - is what catches them.

costModel.note: Least squares of peak resident megabytes on the bytes of the answer space, over the rows that ran, counted their bytes, and could read every file of them. `rows` is that sample rather than the row count. `mbPerFile` and `msPerFile` are the spread the constant could not express. **A row without `cost` never ran** and a row with `corpusUnreadable` above zero has a byte count short by an unknown amount, so neither is in the fit.

sample.note: `planned` is what the run intended to examine, `attempted` what it reached, `measured` what produced a ranking. **`ofAttempted` is the share of reached instances that were measured and `ofPlanned` the share of the protocol**; both are published because a refusal and a row the run never reached are different facts. `worstCaseMap` scores every refusal as zero, so it is a floor on what a run with no bounds at all would have scored, and `standardised` reweights the per-size-band means by the attempted counts so the figure estimates the population it was drawn from rather than the part of it that fitted.

baseline.name: BM25

configuration.tokeniser: lower case, split on non-alphanumerics, then split at camel-case boundaries; tokens shorter than two characters and a stated list of function words are dropped
configuration.document: the answer space file, with its repository-relative path prefixed to its text
configuration.tieBreak: path ascending, so the ranking is a function of the corpus rather than of the directory order

baseline.note: A control variate, not a reproduction of the paper’s BM25 row. Its value is that it measures the instances our analysis cannot run, so the difficulty of the unmeasured half of the corpus is a figure rather than a worry.

crossCheck.name: TF-IDF (cosine)

configuration.termFrequency: sublinear: 1 + ln(tf), so a file that says a word forty times is not forty times about it
configuration.normalisation: L2 over the document vector; cosine against the query vector, so length is divided out
configuration.tokeniser: lower case, split on non-alphanumerics, then split at camel-case boundaries; tokens shorter than two characters and a stated list of function words are dropped
configuration.document: the answer space file, with its repository-relative path prefixed to its text
configuration.tieBreak: path ascending, the same rule as the primary control, so the two differ in weighting alone

crossCheck.note: A second control over the same index, added because the shipped reading was chosen against the first one. It is not a reproduction of the paper’s TF-IDF row either: their tokeniser is a BPE vocabulary and this one is the shared term index, which is stated so the difference is a configuration rather than an assumption.

fallback.name: path + imports (file level)

configuration.document: the answer space file as its repository-relative path followed by the module names of its import statements; **the body is never read**, which is what makes this a second instrument rather than a smaller version of the first
configuration.extractor: one pattern per import form, tested against each line of the head in a fixed order; Python, Java, Kotlin, Scala, Groovy, JavaScript, TypeScript, CommonJS, C#, Rust, C/C++ and Go are recognised and a miss is visible as a zero in `importLines`
configuration.tokeniser: lower case, split on non-alphanumerics, then split at camel-case boundaries; tokens shorter than two characters and a stated list of function words are dropped
configuration.weighting: BM25, k1=1.2, b=0.75, the same arithmetic the control uses
configuration.tieBreak: path ascending, the same rule as the controls

degraded.because: a measured instance contributes its analysis figure, a refused one contributes this fallback’s, and the mean is taken over the union - which is the only reading whose denominator is the protocol

fallback.note: The product degraded rather than declining. `coverage.rows` equals the number of instances that had an answer space to rank, so a mean in `overall` is a mean over the protocol rather than over the part of it that fitted. `pairedVsControl` is a difference of two rankings of the same files; the one asymmetry is the control’s document cap, stated in its own block and in every row as `skippedFiles`.

fileBody.name: whole file body (BM25 over path and text)

configuration.document: the answer space file as its repository-relative path followed by its first 64 KB of text
configuration.scorer: BM25, k1 = 1.2, b = 0.75, the same arithmetic and the same tokeniser as both controls
configuration.tieBreak: path ascending, the same rule as the controls
configuration.note: It equals `bm25` to the last digit wherever the control’s four-thousand-document cap did not bite, because the two read the same text with the same arithmetic; the artifact publishes both so that equality is checkable rather than claimed.

fusionWeights.note: A rung chosen on the rows it is reported over is a rung fitted to them. The selection is made on two splits and read on the third; the gain reported per fold is the held-out one, and a negative gain is a fold where the ladder would have made the product worse.

fusion.name: declarations + path/imports + whole body (reciprocal rank fusion)

configuration.fusion: reciprocal rank fusion, weights "equal" (declarations 1, path/imports 1, body 1), k = 10 (Cormack, Clarke and Büttcher, SIGIR 2009)
arms: the declaration pool, collapsed to files by the shipped aggregation
the file-level arm of `fallback` (path and import statements)
the whole-body arm of `fileBody`, built by the parent and handed to the child
configuration.order: fused after the collapse, because the collapse is a rule over declarations and a file-level ranking has no declarations to collapse
configuration.declined: a refused instance fuses one arm, because the declaration arm is the analysis that was refused; the row says `fused: false` and the count is in `coverage.declined`

fusion.note: On the rows where the analysis ran, `pairedVsDeclarations` is the fusion’s net contribution and is the only figure here in which nothing but the second arm differs. On the rows where it did not, this column declines to the file-level arm and says so per row; the two kinds are never averaged without `coverage` beside them.

configuration.note: The context budget the measurement asked for. **Stated because a figure measured under an unstated budget is a figure about the budget**: a pool of twenty candidates makes the cuts at three, five and ten into three views of the same four files.
units: Retrieved paths are reduced to the corpus's own coordinate system (repository-relative POSIX) before they are scored; the product reports absolute paths because the pipeline is given a root and joins.

Candidates are restricted to the corpus's answer space - non-test files of the configuration's extension, which is the set the published baselines rank. **The filter preserves the retriever's order** and the count it removed is in every row as `outside`.
Average precision reads the first two hundred candidates, which is the pool the product returns. **A shorter list can only lose credit**, so the MAP column is a floor rather than an estimate.

analysisScope.note: The globs the analysis was restricted to, published per row as `analysisScope`. **This run restricted nothing**: every part was written before the field existed, no row carries a scope, and `rowsScoped` is 0. The block states that instead of describing the change the harness can make, because a note about what the code should do is not a note about what this run did. **`null` means the whole checkout**, which is what this artifact measured; a scoped run states its globs here and a mix of the two is refused by `lca-gate.js` rather than averaged here.

space.reason: the indexing pipeline was run without an embedding backend in this job, so the fused list is the lexical list

caveats: The published figures are over all fifty instances per split; this one is over the rows the runner reached, and the measured count is beside it.
Average precision here reads the retriever's own pool of two hundred candidates, which can only lose credit.
The answer arm is not the chat baselines reproduced: it cites from the blocks the retriever selected rather than from the whole path list.
